idea: Pre-IPO and private company primers for crossover funds
buyer: Crossover and public funds looking at private names
pain: Little reliable analysis on private companies before they list
v1: One primer on a named late-stage private company
channel: Her fund network plus husband's IB contacts
verdict: Strong fees and real fit, but private-company information is genuinely scarce and the work is hard to do well.

why.distribution: Her own fund network on the buy side, reinforced by her husband's IB contacts.
why.demand: Crossover funds do commission private-company work; budget exists but is opportunistic.
why.fmf: Her research method transfers, but private companies disclose almost nothing and sourcing is a different craft.
why.revenue_structure: Commissioned one-offs, repeating only when a fund is looking at a new name.
why.defensibility: Sourcing relationships would compound if she built them; she has not yet.
why.leverage: Project work with a reusable framework.
why.time_to_revenue: Sellable within 1-3 months to a known fund.
why.tailwind: Companies staying private longer is a genuine multi-year trend.
why.ceiling: £12k x 17 primers = £204k, which is close to full-time delivery.

ceiling_arithmetic: £12k x 17 primers = £204k gross less data ~£10k. Seventeen primers is essentially a full year of delivery; realistic part-time is 6-8 = £70-95k.
carries: High fees, a real structural trend, and a buyer she can reach directly.
kills: Information scarcity. The work is only as good as the sourcing, and she has no private-market sourcing network yet.
test: Ask three crossover PMs to name a private company they wish they understood, and quote £10k.
test_pass: One names a company and asks for a proposal.
test_fail: They say the information simply is not obtainable.
